title: developer replay workbench — prd seeds
content:
Draft seed notes for a lightweight developer replay workbench (capture + replay + compare) — rough PRD / idea parking lot

Problem statement:
- Debugging inference issues is painful: reproducing a user request requires reconstructing prompts, model version, runtime flags, KV cache, and runtime environment.
- Engineers need a fast way to repro behavioral/regression bugs, measure cost differences across model variants, and iterate without spinning up full infra.
- Current options: ad-hoc logs + manual replays (slow), full e2e infra (heavy), or unit tests (don't capture real runtime shape).

High-level goal:
- Provide a dev-facing workbench that records minimal fidelity traces of inference requests and allows safe, fast local/cloud replays across model variants/configs with side-by-side diffing and cost/latency estimates.

Who cares (primary personas):
- ML infra engineers investigating regressions after a rollout
- Product/feature engineers reproducing user-reported hallucinations or correctness issues
- Performance engineers comparing quantization/packing/seq-len effects
- Solutions/SEs building reproducible demos for customers

User stories (MVP-focused):
1) As an engineer, I can capture a single request trace from hosted API (or local dev runtime) that contains input, model id/version, top-level runtime flags, and minimal metadata (region, token count).
   - Acceptance: one CLI or SDK call creates a named trace that shows in the Workbench UI within 10s.
2) As an engineer, I can replay a captured trace against a different model variant or quantization profile and see output tokens + per-token timestamps and latency.
   - Acceptance: replay UI shows output and a toggled timeline.
3) As an engineer, I can run a diff between original and replayed outputs highlighting inserted/deleted/changed tokens and a simple quality heuristic (e.g., ROUGE-lite or exact-match snippets).
   - Acceptance: diffs are presented inline and downloadable as a small JSON.
4) As an engineer, I can get a cost and latency estimate for the replay using current pricing/billing rates and an infra-simulated p95 latency.
   - Acceptance: display estimated token cost and measured replay latency.
5) As an engineer, I can annotate a trace with notes and tag it (e.g., bug/regression/demo) and share a link to the replay (RBAC controlled).
   - Acceptance: basic metadata and link generation; permissions respect org-level settings.

MVP feature set (minimal scope):
- Capture SDK shim + short CLI: capture metadata (input, model, flags, env), redact sensitive fields by default.
- Workbench UI: list traces, view details, trigger replay, basic diff, annotate.
- Replay harness: lightweight runner that can call hosted API, dedicated pool, or local runtime (pluggable).
- Cost/latency estimator using recent telemetry + pricing lookup.
- Export small JSON replay artifacts and link back to trace.

Nice-to-have (post-MVP):
- KV cache snapshot capture and restore for deterministic long-context replays.
- Batch replays against many model variants and automatic ranking by divergence/cost ratio.
- Replay sandbox for deterministic token-stream stepping and breakpoints.
- Integration with evals harness to attach golden-labels and automated scoring.
- Replay comparison across different routing policies (e.g., fallback path vs primary).

Initial UX sketch (notes-to-self):
- Left pane: trace list (filter by tag/model/user/age)
- Center: trace detail & input + raw output toggle
- Right: replay controls (select target model/config), run, view diff + cost panel
- Quick action: export trace, open terminal replay, create GH issue prefilled with diff snapshot

Privacy & retention guardrails:
- Default: redact PII and user identifiers in captured traces. Provide an allowlist for internal debugging opt-in.
- Retention policy: 30 days by default, configurable by team.
- Audit log: who replayed what and when.

Technical notes / infra constraints:
- Keep captured artifact small (<100KB typical): just prompt, model id, flags, token counts, small sample of response; optional full token stream if user opts in.
- For local deterministic replay, need to capture seed/random state if sampling used. Fallback: force deterministic sampling on replay (top-k + fixed seed) or mark nondeterministic replay.
- Security: when replays hit customer-dedicated infra, ensure workload isolation and RBAC; never escalate privileges.
- Cost estimation: combine token counts with unit prices and add simple overhead multiplier for orchestration.

Key metrics (how we measure success):
- Time-to-repro: median time from trace capture to successful replay (target < 2 minutes end-to-end).
- Reproduction rate: % of traces that can be deterministically reproduced against same model/config (target 80% for deterministic configs).
- Developer adoption: number of engineers using workbench weekly/monthly.
- Bug resolution velocity: reduction in average time to close inference-related tickets.

Open questions / risks:
- How much fidelity do we need to capture to be useful vs. privacy risk? (prompt vs full token stream vs intermediate states)
- How to handle long-context traces with huge token counts? (snapshots + truncation heuristics)
- Storage cost if teams opt into full captures — quota model?
- Determinism: some models + runtime combos are inherently nondeterministic; how to present confidence?
- UI: do we build in Console or in a separate internal app? Reuse Console components for list/detail?

Next steps (short-term):
- Sync with infra (noah) to map which runtime knobs we can reliably capture (seed, sampling, kv snapshot).
- Quick prototype: SDK shim that captures a named trace and uploads to dev bucket (2 day spike).
- Mock a simple web UI with list/detail and manual replay hook that calls hosted API (5 day mock + usability review).
- Put together a short demo for internal infra team and SRE (target: end of next sprint).

Notes / ad-hoc ideas:
- Could reuse existing logging pipeline and add a minimal "trace" schema — cheaper than building new ingestion.
- Support a "replay-as-ci" mode where a trace becomes a regression test that runs nightly across pinned model set.
- For security review: prepare description of fields and default redaction rules.

Random brainlets / TODOs:
- Check whether Dedicated pools can be called from a sandboxed replay runner without breaking isolation.
- Wire pricing endpoint into estimator (who owns price table?).
- UX: quick keyboard shortcut in Console to capture a trace from any API request playback.

-- end of seeds --

(Keeping this intentionally rough — meant to be a lightweight, shareable seed doc to align on scope before formal PRD.)
